In this regime that haven is mislabeled. CPI is 5.1% with the policy rate near zero, so real rates are roughly -5%; the ACTIVE and integrated invariants say exactly what that does: inv-inflation-persistence-tips (w 0.695) favors real assets over nominals, inv-low-real-yields-favor-gold (w 0.428) favors gold over cash AND nominal bonds, and inv-low-real-rate-nominal-bonds marks negative real rates as the condition that clobbers nominal bonds. The tape corroborates: IEF itself is falling (speed -12.1, accel -8.2) — the redirect is selling a weak asset to buy a weak asset, only the second one carries duration into a tightening cycle. Meanwhile commodities (DJP speed +11.2, accel +6.1) are the one rising series on the board and the stack holds none. Second blind spot: the overlay evidently leaves SPY at 50% because it sits above its 200-day line, but SPY's acceleration is -948 — the worst deceleration on the board — so the trend filter is reading position while momentum screams deterioration. A rule that reads two prices and one trend cannot see positioning, policy, or a haven that stops being one when real rates go negative. The book stands; this assessment, and the strategy_revision proposed below, are where the disagreement goes to be measured.

innovation_proposals.title: Make the trend-overlay haven redirect real-rate aware
innovation_proposals.rationale: The market-signal stack's 200-day overlay redirects a below-trend sleeve to 'the haven' (IEF) unconditionally. In February 2022 that rule moved 40% from GLD into intermediate nominal duration with CPI 5.1% and real rates near -5% — the exact condition under which active, integrated invariants (inv-inflation-persistence-tips w 0.695, inv-low-real-yields-favor-gold w 0.428, inv-low-real-rate-nominal-bonds) say nominal bonds underperform inflation hedges. The redirect target itself was falling (IEF speed -12.1). A rule measured over 1991-2021 mostly saw havens that worked in deflationary scares; the 1970s-style negative-real-rate branch is underweighted in that evidence. This revision lets the claim be measured forward in probation instead of argued once.

spec.rule_current: When a sleeve breaches its 200-day trend, redirect its weight to the fixed haven sleeve (IEF).
spec.rule_proposed: When a sleeve breaches its 200-day trend, choose the haven by real-rate regime: if trailing CPI minus the short rate is positive (real rate negative) OR CPI > 4%, redirect to short duration/cash (SHY or cash) or a real-asset sleeve; otherwise redirect to IEF as today.
spec.evidence: CPI 5.1% (Feb 2022), real short rate ~-5%; IEF speed -12.1/accel -8.2 at redirect time; invariants inv-inflation-persistence-tips (market_score 0.818, 9 confirmations), inv-low-real-yields-favor-gold (market_score 0.612, 41 confrontations); ms-stack rolling calmar 0.515, maxDD -23.8%.
spec.scope: market-signal-stack strategy; overlay logic only — the book-selection rule (spread/slope medians) is untouched.
spec.success_metric: Forward paper-mode: revised overlay vs current overlay on rolling Sortino and max drawdown over the next 4 quarters.

innovation_proposals.title: Add a spread-speed confirmation gate to the market-signal credit book selector
innovation_proposals.rationale: This month exposed the gap concretely: the signal reads BAA10Y's LEVEL vs its 10y median (2.34 vs 2.36 — 'tight', by 2bps) while the spread's speed is +0.43/month and accelerating (+0.37). The book chosen assumes spread calm that the derivative says is ending. A level-only threshold at the median boundary is maximally fragile exactly where the decision matters most; the 2022 tape is likely to force a whipsaw re-pick within a quarter, paid for in turnover and slippage the backtest may understate.

spec.current_rule: Select book by credit spread level vs 10y trailing median and yield slope vs its 10y trailing median; apply 200d trend overlay per sleeve.
spec.proposed_rule: When the credit spread sits within +/-10bps of its 10y trailing median, require spread speed <= 0 (or below its own trailing median speed) to enter or hold the 'tight' book; if speed is positive and accelerating, defer to the defensive book one month early. Level remains the primary axis — speed only arbitrates the boundary zone.
evidence: BAA10Y 2022-03-01: level 2.34 vs median 2.36, speed +0.43, acceleration +0.37 — a 'tight' print 2bps from the boundary with a strongly widening derivative
T10Y2Y 0.39 vs median 1.08, speed -0.24: the other signal is unambiguous, so this revision touches only the credit leg
Regime context: stagflation 70.6% confidence with tightening liquidity (speed -0.247) — historically the environment where spreads gap through their medians rather than hover

(2) T10Y2Y at 0.04 is one print from inversion while global liquidity speed is -0.98: the flat-curve bucket here is a tightening artifact, not a neutral state, and the rule has no input for the policy impulse now hitting duration (TLT speed -36, IEF speed -22). innovation_proposals.title: Make the tight-spread book's equity sleeve inflation-regime aware
innovation_proposals.rationale: The market-signal rule picks the equity-heavy book whenever BAA10Y is below its 10y trailing median and the curve is flat, regardless of the inflation quadrant. But the median is nominal: a 1.93% spread is 'loose' against a median minted in a sub-2%-inflation decade, while at CPI ~5.1% it represents negative real compensation — the exact configuration (tight nominal spreads + flat/inverting curve + tightening liquidity, speed -0.98) that preceded the equity drawdowns of 2000-02 and 2007-08, and the ACTIVE invariant 01KY2MY9X0VMVT6FFF2XGBSBGS documents the returns cliff above 5% inflation. This month the rule moved the live book to SPY 50% into a 70.6%-confidence stagflation regime. This is distinct from the two revisions already in probation: the spread-speed confirmation gate (strat-01KZC16RFDQB7XM2NNP4PHB1R5) gates the credit signal's timing, and the real-rate-aware haven redirect (strat-01KZC0STR41Q7VREXBVWH1296Z) governs the haven leg — neither touches the equity sleeve's inflation blindness.

spec.current_rule: Select book from BAA10Y vs 10y trailing median and T10Y2Y vs its 10y trailing median; tight-spread + flat-curve book = SPY 50 / GLD 40 / IWN 10; 200d trend overlay per sleeve.
spec.proposed_change: Add an inflation-regime gate on the equity sleeve of the tight-spread book: when trailing CPI > 4% and rising (or regime detector = falling-growth-rising-inflation with confidence >= 60) AND global liquidity speed < 0, cap the equity sleeve at 25-30% and route the difference to the book's gold sleeve and short/intermediate duration (IEF/SHY), OR equivalently compare BAA10Y in real terms (spread minus trailing CPI) against a real-spread median. Gate is symmetric: it lifts when inflation falls back below threshold.
spec.evidence: CPI ~5.1% with regime stagflation confidence 70.6% at decision date; T10Y2Y 0.04 (one print from inversion); global liquidity speed -0.978; ms-stack retained track: sortino 0.928, calmar 0.439, maxDD -23.8%; in-regime FAVORS sortino 1.615 vs four-seasons-rp 1.967 — the current regime is the instrument's weakest quadrant; invariant 01KY2MY9X0VMVT6FFF2XGBSBGS (ACTIVE): returns fall off a cliff above 5% inflation.
spec.success_metric: In falling-growth-rising-inflation regime windows, revised stack FAVORS sortino/calmar must exceed the unmodified stack's (current: sortino 1.615, calmar 5.89) without degrading its rising-growth-falling-inflation FAVORS (sortino 2.787) by more than 10% over probation.

innovation_proposals.title: Apply the 200-day trend overlay to the GLD sleeve, not only the equity sleeve
innovation_proposals.rationale: This month the overlay correctly redirected SPY 50 → IEF 50, but the same book keeps GLD 40 untouched while gold is itself deteriorating (GLD speed -167, acceleration -160 at 2022-05-02) and real yields are backing up (DGS10 speed +0.54). A 40% haven sleeve that is never trend-checked is a blind spot: in a real-yield backup, gold can fall alongside equities (as in 2013 and March 2022), and the rule as built would hold it through the whole drawdown. Making the overlay symmetric — redirect GLD to SHY/cash when GLD is below its own 200d trend — is a rule-level claim that should be measured in probation, not applied on this cycle's conviction.

spec.proposed_rule: Apply the same 200-day trend check to GLD: when GLD closes below its 200-day average, redirect the GLD sleeve to SHY (or cash) until it recovers. IWN sleeve unchanged (already small and capped).

innovation_proposals.title: Add a spread-speed early-warning note to the tight-spread book's holding period
innovation_proposals.rationale: The book selector reads BAA10Y level vs its 10y median (2.06 vs 2.32 — tight) but ignores the spread's own momentum: BAA10Y speed is +0.12 to +0.15 with acceleration +0.44 to +0.53, i.e. the spread is widening quickly from a tight level. A book chosen on a tight-spread reading can be one month from its own exit condition and the rule neither sees nor warns about it. The proposal is not to change selection, but to emit an early-warning flag when spread speed exceeds its own trailing norm, so the owner placing manual orders knows the book's premise is decaying. A warning layer is a weaker claim than a gate and can earn FAVORS on its own merits.

spec.current_rule: Book selection uses BAA10Y level vs 10y trailing median and T10Y2Y level vs its median; no use of spread speed/acceleration.
spec.proposed_rule: Compute BAA10Y 3-month speed; when it exceeds +1 standard deviation of its trailing 10y speed distribution while the tight-spread book is in force, attach an 'early-warning: spread widening' flag to the monthly decision output shown to the owner. Selection unchanged.
evidence: T10Y2Y 0.19-0.22, within weeks of inversion at current speed +0.15
spec.expected_effect: Owner sees premise decay one to two months before the level-based rule flips books; no change to backtested selection logic.
